body:
Current throughput and coding-model guidance; repository instructions and actual resource grants govern. Superseded queue, stopped-session assignments and old landing exceptions are not current authority.

Greg via Advisor#1319,2026-10-13T02:44Z, verbatim: "Greg confirms Codex gpt-6.1-sol is the preferred implementation model. Apply it by default to every new coder assignment. Use a different model only when Sol is unavailable or moving already-started work would cost more than continuing it; record that exception. Do not interrupt Merger's current w-b411 design review merely to swap its model."
Greg via Advisor#1739,2026-10-18T21:14Z, verbatim: "keep agents continuously coding on ready, independent slices; use capacity for implementation, not repeated status/design turns. TermAl owns test runs; workers consume pass/fail metadata and bounded failure excerpts only, never routine full logs. Use architects exceptionally: only a real architecture-boundary change, durable-format question, or unresolved design conflict. Otherwise coordinator/implementer decides and proceeds. Apply to Engram lanes and report active coding count at boundaries."

The Coder prepares code and author tests; integration validates the final combined input under current rules. Independent coding is not capped by serial gate scheduling. Resource/quiet windows follow current rules-central-slot and rules-remote-test-runs, not historic numeric budgets.

Kimi fallback source, Greg's exact words via Advisor#1430 (2026-10-15): "claude will soon run of tokens / we need to use Kimi as replacement / and focus on simple cleanup / we have enormous backlog". The adopted Codex-or-Claude stand-in clause landed d10f724; current AGENTS/CLAUDE govern one stand-in, never both reviewers. This gives no standing model-capacity assumption or permission to bypass a required review.
